subject.title: Dashboard: ops widgets — agent status + approvals queue

question: Should this ops-widget layer land as a stacked dashboard feature with widget-scoped approvals, or should maintainers require the foundation, storage, security, and broader approval-scope decisions to be resolved first?
rationale: The PR's core idea is product-relevant, but accepting it also commits OpenClaw to a new dashboard persistence model, agent-authored widget security boundary, dependency graph change, and approval UX scope that automation cannot safely choose.

options.title: Fix and prove before merge
options.body: Require the contributor to rebase after the foundation stack, fix the current blockers, move persistence to SQLite/plugin state, and add real browser proof plus security/dependency authorization before reconsidering merge.

options.title: Accept narrower approvals scope
options.body: Maintainers can explicitly accept the widget-only approval surface as a first slice, but should leave broader exec/plugin approval asks tracked separately.

options.title: Pause this stack layer
options.body: Close or pause this PR if the current modular-dashboard stack is not the desired product/security direction for OpenClaw core.

recommendation.title: Fix and prove before merge
recommendation.body: Require the contributor to rebase after the foundation stack, fix the current blockers, move persistence to SQLite/plugin state, and add real browser proof plus security/dependency authorization before reconsidering merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The history links @steipete most strongly to the Control UI plugin seam and database-first plugin-state direction involved in this choice.
